title: Feature request: Connect Claude code to Claude projects
body:
Feature Request: Integrate Claude Code with Claude.ai Projects Knowledge Bases

Summary

Enable Claude Code to access and leverage knowledge bases from Claude.ai Projects, allowing developers to use their existing project documentation, specifications, and reference materials directly within their coding workflows.

Current State
- Claude.ai Projects allow users to upload documents and create knowledge bases that Claude can reference within 
- Projects offer caching benefits where uploaded documents are cached for future use, and only new/uncached portions count against usage limits [[(1)](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/10167454-using-the-github-integration)](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/10167454-using-the-github-integration)
- Claude Code currently supports project-specific configurations using `.claude/settings.json` files and custom slash commands [[(2)](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/blob/main/README.md)](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/blob/main/README.md)
- CLAUDE.md files can link other Markdown and text files, which are automatically pulled into context [[(2)](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/blob/main/README.md)](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/blob/main/README.md)

### Proposed Enhancement
Allow Claude Code to connect to and access Claude.ai Projects knowledge bases, enabling:

1. **Seamless Knowledge Integration**: Access existing project documentation, API specs, design documents, and other reference materials stored in Projects
2. **Efficient Caching**: Leverage the existing Projects caching system to avoid repeatedly processing the same documents
3. **Unified Workflow**: Maintain context across both web-based Claude interactions and terminal-based Claude Code sessions
4. **Enhanced Context**: Provide Claude Code with richer project understanding through comprehensive knowledge bases

### Use Cases
- **API Development**: Access API documentation and specifications while implementing endpoints
- **Code Refactoring**: Reference architectural decisions and design patterns stored in Projects
- **Bug Fixes**: Consult troubleshooting guides and known issues documentation
- **Feature Implementation**: Access product requirements and user stories during development
- **Code Reviews**: Reference coding standards and best practices from project documentation

### Benefits
- **Reduced Context Switching**: Developers can access project knowledge without leaving their terminal
- **Improved Code Quality**: Better context leads to more informed coding decisions
- **Cost Efficiency**: Leverage existing Projects caching to reduce token usage
- **Consistency**: Ensure Claude Code has the same project context as web-based Claude sessions

### Implementation Suggestions
- Add a configuration option to link Claude Code sessions to specific Claude.ai Projects
- Extend the `.claude/settings.json` format to include project references
- Provide commands to sync or refresh project knowledge within Claude Code
- Consider integration with the existing CLAUDE.md linking mechanism

### Technical Considerations
- Maintain security and access controls consistent with Projects permissions
- Handle offline scenarios gracefully when project knowledge isn't accessible
- Provide clear indicators when project knowledge is being used vs. local context

This feature would significantly enhance Claude Code's capabilities by combining the power of local development tools with the rich knowledge management features of Claude.ai Projects.
author: salimmallick

top_comments.body: I strongly endorse this feature. I commonly will use Claude projects to help me organize my brainstorming and feature planning and development. I often do this on my mobile device when I'm not near my computer or terminal sometimes I'll do it on the go. It would be really helpful if Claude code was able to have up-to-date knowledge about my brainstorming sessions that I develop on the Claude app and linked to a project.
